## Read this first: one known defect

The long-conversion path still miscompiles a cast of a shifted `long` in a
condition. This is an open correctness gap, despite the rest of the 32-bit
`long` work being complete.

Reproduction:

```c
int main(void) {
    long v = 70000;
    if ((int)(v >> 16) != 1) return 1;
    if ((int)v != 4464) return 2;
    return 0;
}
```

Observed on this tree:

```text
kr16 build ... && kr16 vm ...
exit 1
```

So `(int)(v >> 16)` does not produce 1. Earlier investigation found the
simple-condition path emitting a 16-bit compare instead of the long shift/cast
path; the `uses_long` rejection and Cast dispatch were added, but this exact
case still fails. Fix this before treating item 2 as fully complete:

- add a regression test for `(int)(long_expr >> 16)` and `(int)long_expr`
- trace `expression_type` through the cast/shift parse tree
- verify the simple-condition emitter rejects the whole tree

The standalone reproduction is not committed.

## Completed work in this span

### 1. C runtime error/stdio layer

- `errno`, `strerror`, host-service status mapping
- `fscanf`, `freopen`, `tmpfile`, buffered interactive stdin
- tests for error codes, EOF, partial reads/writes, format parsing

### 2. 32-bit `long` / `long long`

Implemented:

- 4-byte storage and `sizeof`
- arithmetic, divide/modulo, shifts, bitwise, comparisons
- assignment, compound assignment, `++`/`--`, unary `-`/`~`
- two-word stack ABI for long-interface functions
- `printf` `%ld`, `%lu`, `%lx`, `%lo`
- `fscanf` `%ld`, `%lu`, `%lx`
- long negation borrow fix

Known gap: the cast-of-shift issue above.

Long ABI convention, for future work:

- long expression result: `R0` low, `R1` high
- functions with any long parameter or return use all-stack arguments
- caller pushes reverse; long is high word then low word
- callee reads all parameters from `[R4+4...]`
- long return in `R0`/`R1`

### 3. Linker hardening

- relocatable `-r` links (`LinkOptions::relocatable`, `kr16 ld -r`)
- weak symbols (`SymbolBinding::Weak`, assembler `.weak`)
- strong definitions override weak; undefined weak resolves to 0
- common symbols (`SymbolBinding::Common`, assembler `.comm`)
- common allocation in `.bss`
- tests for all three

### 4. Debugger/DAP

Existing handlers were verified and covered:

- `readMemory`
- `disassemble`
- `evaluate`
- `setFunctionBreakpoints`

Remaining DAP deferrals: threaded console/DAP coordination and live VSIX
marketplace publishing.

### 5. Release engineering
